name: Melanotan II
summary: Injectable peptide that boosts melanin production for a deeper tan with less sun, and also raises libido and lowers appetite.

name: Afamelanotide
summary: Prescription melanocortin implant that darkens skin through added melanin; approved for a rare light-sensitivity disorder, not for cosmetic tanning.

name: Canthaxanthin
summary: Carotenoid pigment taken in oral tanning pills that tints skin orange-brown from the inside; linked to retinal deposits.

name: Tretinoin
summary: Prescription vitamin A cream that speeds skin renewal and builds collagen, clearing acne and smoothing fine lines and uneven tone.

name: Tazarotene
summary: Prescription retinoid regarded as among the most potent topicals, used for stubborn acne and photoaging lines and mottled tone.

name: Isotretinoin
summary: Oral retinoid that shrinks oil glands to clear severe acne, often for long-lasting results and less scarring.

name: Botulinum toxin A
summary: Injected muscle relaxer that smooths frown, forehead and eye-corner lines and is also used to slim the jaw.

name: Hydroquinone
summary: Prescription skin lightener that fades dark spots, melasma and acne marks for a more even skin tone.

name: Spironolactone
summary: Prescription antiandrogen that reduces oil and clears hormonal acne, also used for hair and body-hair concerns.

name: Clascoterone
summary: Topical antiandrogen cream approved for acne, clearing breakouts without systemic hormone effects; studied for hair loss.

name: PDRN / Polynucleotides
summary: DNA-fragment skin boosters, injected or topical, used for skin quality, scars and post-procedure recovery.

name: Semaglutide
summary: Weekly GLP-1 medication that cuts appetite and drives large fat loss, leaning out the body and face together.

name: Tirzepatide
summary: Weekly GIP/GLP-1 injection with the largest average weight losses reported for an approved drug, leaning out body and face.

name: Liraglutide
summary: Daily GLP-1 injection that curbs appetite for fat loss, a milder and older option than semaglutide.

name: Retatrutide
summary: Investigational weekly triple-agonist (GLP-1/GIP/glucagon) with very large trial weight losses that people want for leaning out.

name: Cagrilintide
summary: Weekly amylin-analogue injection that boosts fullness and lowers food intake, trialled alone and with semaglutide as CagriSema.

name: Setmelanotide
summary: MC4R-targeting injection that reduces hunger and weight in people with specific rare genetic obesity conditions.

name: Tesamorelin
summary: Prescription growth-hormone-releasing peptide that reduces visceral belly fat, approved for HIV-related abdominal fat.

name: AOD-9604
summary: Growth-hormone fragment sold as a research peptide for fat loss without full growth-hormone effects.

name: HGH Fragment 176-191
summary: Growth-hormone fragment sold as a research chemical to mobilise fat for cutting, without growth effects.

name: 5-Amino-1MQ
summary: Small-molecule NNMT inhibitor sold to raise fat metabolism and reduce body fat; studied in cells and mice.

name: Testosterone
summary: The main male hormone, behind muscle, bone and masculine features, used medically for deficiency and in physique culture.

name: Somatropin
summary: Prescription growth hormone used for body composition, with fuller, leaner physique effects and facial changes with chronic excess.

name: MK-677
summary: Oral ghrelin mimic that raises growth hormone and IGF-1 for recovery, sleep and appetite to help bulking.

name: CJC-1295
summary: Injectable GHRH peptide users take to raise growth hormone for recovery, sleep, leanness and skin.

name: Ipamorelin
summary: Selective GH-releasing peptide users take for recovery, sleep and hoped-for height, often alongside CJC-1295.

name: Sermorelin
summary: GHRH peptide that prompts your own growth hormone release, used off-label for recovery, leanness and anti-ageing.

name: GHRP-6
summary: GH-releasing peptide that raises growth hormone and causes intense hunger, used by lifters for bulking and recovery.

name: IGF-1 LR3
summary: Modified IGF-1 analogue sold to bodybuilders for muscle growth and repair.

name: Follistatin-344
summary: Injectable follistatin product sold to block myostatin and build muscle beyond natural limits.

name: Ostarine
summary: SARM lifters use for lean mass and a leaner look, trialled for muscle wasting.

name: LGD-4033
summary: SARM lifters use to add lean mass in a few weeks with less perceived hormonal impact than steroids.

name: RAD-140
summary: Potent SARM lifters use for muscle and fat loss, with liver and hormone effects reported.

name: YK-11
summary: Steroid-like SARM marketed as a myostatin inhibitor for gains beyond ordinary SARMs.

name: Finasteride
summary: Approved oral DHT blocker that slows male pattern hair loss and helps keep your hairline and thickness.

name: Dutasteride
summary: Stronger DHT blocker than finasteride, used off-label to stop male pattern hair loss.

name: Bimatoprost
summary: Prescription eyelash-growth drop (Latisse) that gives longer, thicker, darker lashes for a more defined eye area, and is sometimes used on brows.

name: Pyrilutamide
summary: Topical androgen-receptor blocker developed for pattern hair loss, used as a local alternative to oral DHT blockers to keep scalp hair.

name: RU58841
summary: Topical antiandrogen used by hair-loss communities as a scalp-only alternative to finasteride, to slow miniaturisation and keep hair.

name: Teriparatide
summary: Prescription bone-building injection for osteoporosis that is discussed in bone-focused circles for jaw and facial structure.

name: Romosozumab
summary: Sclerostin-blocking osteoporosis antibody that builds bone, mentioned in bone-focused circles for facial structure.

name: BPC-157
summary: Healing peptide used by lifters to recover from tendon and muscle injuries so training stays consistent; research is mainly animal.

name: TB-500
summary: Research peptide stacked with BPC-157 for faster soft-tissue recovery; what vendors sell under the name varies.

name: KPV
summary: Short anti-inflammatory peptide from alpha-MSH, promoted for calmer, less irritated skin and gut without tanning.

name: Thymosin alpha-1
summary: Immune-modulating peptide used in peptide stacks, with some users hoping for a healthier, younger look; human research covers medical conditions.

name: Rapamycin
summary: Prescription mTOR inhibitor used off-label by longevity enthusiasts to slow aging, with topical versions explored for skin rejuvenation.

name: Metformin
summary: Diabetes drug used off-label for belly fat, carb handling, acne and anti-aging, and to manage blood sugar during hormone use.

name: Epitalon
summary: Synthetic peptide promoted for telomere lengthening and slower aging, which users connect to a younger look.

name: MOTS-c
summary: Mitochondria-derived peptide used as an exercise mimetic, aimed at fat loss and leaner body composition.

name: SS-31
summary: Mitochondria-targeted peptide used for cellular energy, skin anti-aging and wound healing; approved only for Barth syndrome.

name: Furosemide
summary: Prescription loop diuretic that some people misuse off-label to drop water weight for a leaner, less puffy look.

name: Bremelanotide
summary: PT-141 (Vyleesi), an Rx melanocortin peptide approved for low desire in premenopausal women; some men discuss it with tanning peptides, and pigment spotting is a known effect.

name: Dersimelagon
summary: An investigational oral pill that switches on the MC1R pigment receptor to darken skin; tanning-focused circles follow it, though it was developed for light-sensitivity disorders.

name: Semax
summary: A Russian ACTH-derived nootropic peptide used in study-maxxing circles for focus and learning; it is not an appearance compound, and human trials are small stroke studies.

name: Trifarotene (Aklief)
summary: Aklief is a prescription retinoid cream approved in 2019 for acne on the face and trunk, backed by large vehicle-controlled trials.

name: Poly-L-lactic acid (Sculptra)
summary: Sculptra is an injectable PLLA collagen stimulator that rebuilds cheek and midface volume gradually, with effects lasting up to about two years in trials.

name: Deoxycholic acid (Kybella)
summary: Kybella is an injectable approved for double chins that dissolves fat cells under the chin for a sharper chin-neck line without surgery.

name: Polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA) filler
summary: Permanent filler beads (Artefill, Bellafill) that add lasting volume to cheeks and chin or lift acne scars; removal can be difficult.

name: Poly-D,L-lactic acid (PDLLA)
summary: A collagen-stimulating injectable related to PLLA, used for firmer, smoother skin, wrinkles and scar texture, with results building over weeks.

name: Collagen filler
aka: Zyderm, Zyplast, bovine or human collagen filler
summary: The original injectable filler, used to plump lines, folds and lips with visible results right away; temporary, and now largely replaced by hyaluronic acid.

name: Polyacrylamide gel
summary: A permanent synthetic gel filler used for facial contouring and HIV-related facial fat loss; volume shows once placed, and removal can be difficult.

name: Mercury skin lightening
summary: Mercury-salt creams and soaps that pale skin by blocking melanin; banned in many countries but still found in informal markets, with serious toxicity.

name: Clobetasol propionate
summary: A super-potent prescription steroid cream that turns up undeclared in illicit lightening creams, where skin paling is a side effect; documented skin harms are significant.

name: Trenbolone
summary: A potent veterinary-origin steroid used by bodybuilders for muscle mass and a dry, hard, vascular look; reviews of users report adverse effects in most.

name: Nandrolone
summary: An injectable steroid (Deca) used by lifters for muscle size and joint comfort; trials show lean-mass gains in sick patients, none in healthy lifters.

name: Oxandrolone
summary: Anavar, a mild oral steroid used to stay lean while dieting by holding on to muscle for a harder-looking physique.

name: Stanozolol
summary: Winstrol, a doping-famous steroid used for a dry, lean, hard look; approved for hereditary angioedema, with notable HDL and liver effects.

name: Boldenone
summary: Equipoise, a veterinary steroid bodybuilders use for slow, steady lean mass gain and fuller muscle; no human trials exist.

name: Methandienone
summary: Dianabol, the classic oral bulking steroid; small controlled trials show lean mass gain, with liver, blood-pressure and hormonal costs.

name: Oxymetholone
summary: Anadrol, an anemia drug that bodybuilders use as a potent oral bulker for mass and fullness, with well-documented liver effects.

name: Drostanolone
summary: Masteron, a DHT-derived injectable used by bodybuilders for a dry, hard, defined look; historically a breast-cancer drug.

name: Mesterolone
summary: Proviron, a mild oral DHT derivative used medically for hypogonadism and fertility, and by users as an add-on for hardness and libido.

name: Methyltestosterone
aka: 17-alpha-methyltestosterone, MT, Android, Methitest, Estratest (with esterified estrogens)
summary: An early oral testosterone analogue still used medically for hypogonadism and menopause, with little documented use for muscle or looks.

name: Fluoxymesterone
summary: Halotestin, a strong oral androgen that bodybuilders add for hardness, strength and aggression; trials are in breast cancer and hypogonadism.

name: Methenolone
summary: Primobolan, a mild DHT-derived steroid prized in bodybuilding for lean gains with fewer side effects; human trials are in anemia, cancer and rehabilitation.

name: Trestolone (MENT)
summary: Trestolone (MENT), an experimental potent androgen built for male contraception and replacement, discussed on looksmax forums for muscle and topical jawline ideas.

name: Dimethandrolone undecanoate
summary: DMAU, an experimental oral androgen-progestin built as a male contraceptive pill; forum users speculate about muscle, with no human data on it.

name: Methasterone
summary: Superdrol, an oral designer steroid once sold as a supplement; users report fast lean muscle gain, while case reports document liver and kidney injury.

name: Androstenedione
summary: A weak natural androgen once sold as the 1990s baseball-era testosterone-booster supplement; trials found no strength or muscle gains at ordinary doses.

name: Dihydrotestosterone (DHT)
summary: The potent androgen behind puberty changes; DHT gel is used on forums hoping for a more masculine face, beard and penis size.

name: Human chorionic gonadotropin (hCG)
summary: The pregnancy hormone that fertility clinics and TRT doctors use to keep the testes working; forum claims for face, height and penis growth are untested.

name: Andarine (S-4)
summary: An unapproved SARM from the early 2000s that users take during cuts to hold on to muscle; only animal data exist, and yellow-green vision is widely reported.

name: Cardarine (GW501516)
summary: A discontinued metabolic drug sold as a fat-loss and endurance aid; small trials showed lipid benefits, and rodent cancer findings ended its development.

name: SR9009 (Stenabolic)
summary: A REV-ERB clock-receptor agonist sold as Stenabolic for endurance and cutting; research is in cells and animals, with a liver-injury case report.

name: CJC-1295 with DAC
summary: A long-acting growth hormone-releasing peptide that users stack with ipamorelin, aiming for a leaner, more muscular look, better recovery and skin.

name: Modified GRF (1-29)
summary: A short-acting GHRH analogue (CJC-1295 without DAC) paired with GH-releasing peptides in stacks for better recovery, muscle and a leaner look.

name: GHRP-2 (Pralmorelin)
summary: A potent ghrelin-receptor peptide that triggers growth hormone release, used by peptide users for muscle, recovery and sleep; a diagnostic test drug in Japan.

name: Hexarelin (Examorelin)
summary: A potent growth hormone-releasing peptide used alone or with a GHRH analogue for muscle gain with less water retention, studied for hormone release since the 1990s.

name: Bimagrumab
summary: An investigational antibody that blocks muscle's growth brakes; trials show fat loss with lean mass kept or gained, but it is not available outside studies.

name: Survodutide
summary: An investigational once-weekly glucagon/GLP-1 injection in phase 3 that cuts appetite and raises energy use, leading to lower body fat; not yet approved.

name: VK2735
summary: An investigational weekly GLP-1/GIP injection (oral form in trials) in phase 3; phase 2 showed about 9 to 15% weight loss in 13 weeks.

name: CagriSema
summary: A not-yet-approved weekly semaglutide plus cagrilintide shot that cut weight about 20% in phase 3 trials, bringing lower body fat.

name: Exenatide
summary: The original GLP-1 injection, approved for type 2 diabetes in 2005, which curbs appetite and brings modest weight loss; later GLP-1 drugs are stronger.

name: Tesofensine
summary: An unapproved oral appetite suppressant that blocks dopamine, noradrenaline and serotonin reuptake; a 24-week trial found 4.5% to 10.6% extra weight loss over placebo.

name: Naltrexone/Bupropion (Contrave)
summary: A prescription pill pairing an opioid blocker with an antidepressant to curb appetite and cravings, giving solid but modest weight loss next to GLP-1 drugs.

name: Phentermine
summary: A decades-old prescription stimulant appetite suppressant used for short-term cutting, with modest weight loss and cardiovascular warnings.

name: Phentermine/Topiramate (Qsymia)
summary: A once-daily phentermine plus topiramate capsule for chronic weight management, with clear weight loss over placebo, behind GLP-1 injections.

name: Clenbuterol
summary: An asthma-drug stimulant used as a gray-market cutting pill for a leaner, more defined look, with a documented record of heart problems.

name: 2,4-Dinitrophenol (DNP)
summary: A 1930s diet drug that turns cells into heaters for very fast fat loss; it is banned for human use because the gap between effective and dangerous doses is narrow.

name: Ephedrine
aka: ECA stack (ephedrine, caffeine, aspirin), ma huang
summary: The stimulant in the classic ECA stack, used for appetite suppression and energy while cutting; it raises pulse and pressure, and the FDA banned it from supplements.

name: Sibutramine
summary: A withdrawn prescription appetite suppressant that helped people lose a few extra kilograms but raised cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients.

name: Baricitinib
summary: A prescription JAK-inhibitor pill approved for severe alopecia areata that regrows patchy or total hair loss; not approved for ordinary pattern baldness.

name: Flutamide
summary: A prostate-cancer antiandrogen that some people use off-label to slow androgen-driven hair thinning and keep more scalp hair; liver toxicity is its main limit.

name: Bicalutamide
summary: A prostate-cancer antiandrogen used off-label to slow female pattern hair loss and reduce androgen effects on hair follicles; carries a liver-injury warning.

name: Cyproterone acetate
summary: A progestin-antiandrogen prescribed to women for hirsutism, severe acne and androgen-related hair loss; meningioma and liver risks limit long-term use.

name: Latanoprost
summary: A glaucoma eye drop whose labelled side effects include longer, thicker, darker lashes and darker irises, which is why it comes up for lashes and eye colour.

name: Anastrozole
summary: A breast-cancer aromatase inhibitor that teen heightmaxxers discuss for keeping growth plates open and TRT users for oestrogen control; no trials show a height gain in healthy people.

name: Letrozole
summary: A potent aromatase inhibitor used for breast cancer and fertility that heightmaxxers consider for delaying growth plates; no trials in healthy teens exist.

name: Exemestane
summary: A steroidal breast-cancer aromatase inhibitor that teen heightmaxxers favour as the milder option for keeping growth plates open; no trials in healthy adolescents.

name: Tamoxifen
summary: A breast-cancer oestrogen-receptor blocker that bodybuilders and TRT users take to treat or prevent gynecomastia for a leaner, more defined chest.

name: Clomiphene
summary: A fertility drug that men use off-label to lift their own testosterone without injections, for more muscle and leanness; studied in hypogonadal men, not for looks.

name: Enclomiphene
summary: The trans-isomer of clomiphene, studied for raising testosterone in men with secondary hypogonadism while preserving fertility; forum appearance and height use is untested.

name: Topical finasteride
aka: Finasteride spray / solution / gel; compounded finasteride-minoxidil
summary: Scalp-applied finasteride that blocks scalp DHT to slow hair loss and hold your hairline, with less whole-body exposure than the pill.

name: Fluridil
summary: Topical antiandrogen sold in Europe as Eucapil that blocks androgen receptors in the scalp to slow pattern hair thinning.

name: Kisspeptin
summary: Hypothalamic peptide that triggers LH release; TRT forums use kisspeptin-10 as an hCG alternative to keep the testes active.

name: Gonadorelin
summary: Synthetic GnRH that TRT users take instead of hCG to keep the testes active and limit shrinkage while on testosterone.

name: Liothyronine (T3)
summary: Prescription thyroid hormone that some cutters use off-label to speed fat loss; the US label carries a boxed warning against that use.

name: Hyaluronic acid filler
summary: The standard reversible injectable gel that adds volume to lips, cheeks, chin, jaw and under-eyes, with visible results right away.

name: Glutathione (IV)
summary: Injected antioxidant offered in some clinics as a skin-lightening drip, based on lab findings about melanin; reviews flag anaphylaxis and liver risks.

name: Psoralen (PUVA, bergamot oil tanning)
summary: A plant-derived light-sensitizer that makes skin tan more strongly under UVA; used medically as PUVA, but withdrawn from tanning products in 1996.

name: Nasal tanning spray
summary: Needle-free melanotan-style sprays sold online to darken skin without sun; unlicensed products with no published nasal-route study.

name: Hydroquinone-tretinoin-steroid triple cream (Kligman formula)
aka: Kligman formula, triple combination cream, Tri-Luma (fluocinolone/hydroquinone/tretinoin)
summary: The classic prescription melasma cream combining hydroquinone, tretinoin and a steroid to fade dark patches.

name: Oral antibiotics (doxycycline/minocycline)
summary: Prescription tetracycline pills that calm inflamed acne and rosacea for clearer, less red skin; a standard dermatology option with known side effects.

name: Topical clindamycin
aka: Cleocin T, Dalacin T; combos: BenzaClin, Duac, Acanya, Ziana
summary: A prescription antibiotic gel or lotion, usually paired with benzoyl peroxide, that reduces inflamed pimples for clearer skin.

name: Dapsone gel (Aczone)
summary: A prescription anti-inflammatory gel that calms red, inflamed acne, often chosen when other topicals irritate; studied in large phase 3 trials.

name: Sarecycline (Seysara)
summary: A once-daily prescription tetracycline approved in 2018 to clear inflammatory acne on the face, and often the body too.

name: Combined oral contraceptive pill
aka: The pill, COC, OCP; acne-approved brands include Ortho Tri-Cyclen, Estrostep, Beyaz and YAZ
summary: The estrogen-plus-progestin birth control pill, also prescribed to women for hormonal acne because it lowers free androgens and oil production.

name: Topical estrogen (estriol) cream
summary: Mild estrogen cream used for thicker, firmer, smoother skin, mainly by older users, as an off-label use of a menopausal hormone ingredient.

name: Metronidazole / ivermectin (rosacea creams)
summary: Prescription creams that calm the bumps and inflammation of rosacea for a clearer, less irritated face; best studied for papules and pustules rather than flat redness.

name: Brimonidine gel (Mirvaso)
summary: A prescription gel that narrows facial blood vessels to visibly reduce rosacea redness within hours; the effect is temporary, and rebound redness has been reported.

name: Oxymetazoline cream (Rhofade)
summary: A prescription cream approved in 2017 that narrows facial blood vessels to reduce persistent rosacea redness for a calmer, more even-looking complexion.

name: Hyaluronidase filler dissolving
aka: Hylenex, Vitrase, Amphadase, Hydase, filler dissolver
summary: An enzyme that breaks down hyaluronic acid, used to dissolve lumpy, bluish or overfilled filler, notably under the eyes.

name: Antibiotics (doxycycline) for back acne
summary: A prescription tetracycline antibiotic widely used for inflamed back and body acne, typically in short courses alongside non-antibiotic treatments.

name: Oxymetazoline eye drops (Upneeq)
summary: A prescription 0.1% oxymetazoline eye drop approved for acquired ptosis that briefly lifts the upper lid for a more open, awake look.

name: Botox nose tip lift
aka: Nasal tip Botox, depressor septi nasi injection
summary: Botulinum toxin in the muscle that pulls the nasal tip down, a temporary off-label way to lift a drooping tip, especially when smiling.

name: Hyaluronidase lip filler dissolving
summary: An enzyme injected to break down hyaluronic acid filler, letting lips be corrected or reset when filler looks lumpy, uneven or overfilled.

name: PLLA / Sculptra perioral
summary: An injectable collagen stimulator used around the mouth to soften lines and gradually rebuild volume over weeks.

name: TMJ Botox
aka: Botulinum toxin for TMD, masseter / lateral pterygoid Botox
summary: Botulinum toxin injected into jaw muscles to relax clenching and jaw pain, with masseter treatment also giving some users a slimmer lower face.

name: Tretinoin for scalp
summary: A retinoid that hair-loss users mix into minoxidil hoping for better absorption and fuller regrowth.

name: Cetirizine topical
summary: An antihistamine lotion explored for hair loss, aimed at protecting follicles from shrinking, tested in a small trial in women.

name: Setipiprant
summary: An experimental PGD2-receptor blocker, moved from allergy research to hair loss, that did not beat placebo in its phase 2a trial.

name: Platelet PGD2 inhibitors
aka: DP2/CRTH2 antagonists, PGD2 pathway blockers, setipiprant
summary: An experimental hair-loss approach that blocks prostaglandin D2 signalling to free miniaturised follicles to regrow.

name: Ritlecitinib (Litfulo)
summary: Prescription daily pill that regrows hair lost in patches from severe alopecia areata; not for pattern baldness and carries a boxed warning.

name: Verteporfin hair
summary: An eye-disease drug that forum users follow as a possible route to scarless hair transplants and regrowth in scar tissue.

name: Oral cyproterone acetate
summary: Prescription antiandrogen used abroad by women for hair loss, acne and excess body hair, with liver, clot and meningioma risks.

name: Tretinoin for beard
summary: Prescription tretinoin added to minoxidil routines on the theory that it boosts absorption and beard growth.

name: Clomiphene / enclomiphene
summary: An oral fertility SERM used off-label by men to raise their own testosterone for muscle and beard goals; studied in hypogonadal men, not for looks.

name: hCG
summary: A prescription LH-mimicking hormone used alongside testosterone to keep the testes active; established in medicine, unstudied for looks.

name: Eflornithine (Vaniqa)
summary: Prescription cream that slows facial hair regrowth in women so less shaving or plucking is needed; it works only while used.

name: Leuprolide (GnRH agonist puberty blocker)
summary: A prescription GnRH agonist that pauses puberty in medical settings; height-focused users discuss it as a way to keep growth plates open longer.

name: Mazdutide
summary: A weekly GLP-1 and glucagon dual-agonist injection, approved in China for weight loss, used to get leaner by cutting appetite and raising energy use.

name: Orforglipron
summary: A once-daily GLP-1 pill that is not a peptide, taken to cut appetite and body fat for a leaner look without injections.

name: Oral semaglutide (Rybelsus)
summary: Semaglutide as a daily tablet that lowers appetite for fat loss; Rybelsus is approved for type 2 diabetes and a weight-loss version is approved in the US.

name: Lipo-C / MIC B12 injections
aka: MIC B12, Lipo-B, lipotropic injections, fat-burner shots
summary: A clinic-administered B12 plus lipotropic (methionine, inositol, choline) shot that people add to a diet in pursuit of leaner body composition and more energy.

name: Compounded semaglutide / microdosing GLP-1
aka: Semaglutide microdosing, low-dose GLP-1, compounded sema
summary: Pharmacy-made or gray-market semaglutide, often used at below-label amounts, to cut appetite and body fat for a leaner face and body.

name: Peg-MGF (mechano growth factor)
summary: A pegylated synthetic version of the IGF-1Ec peptide sold as a research chemical that bodybuilders use hoping to add muscle.

name: Insulin (bodybuilding use)
summary: A prescription diabetes hormone that some bodybuilders use hoping to drive nutrients into muscle for fuller, bigger muscles; hypoglycemia is the main danger.

name: Prohormones (1-Andro, 4-AD)
summary: Steroid precursors once sold over the counter as testosterone boosters for muscle and strength; androstenedione has been a controlled substance in the US since 2005.

name: Testosterone replacement therapy
summary: Medical testosterone that restores normal levels in hypogonadism, with virilizing effects such as more muscle and a deeper voice.

name: Testosterone cypionate
summary: Long-acting injectable testosterone labelled for hypogonadism, with voice deepening among its listed virilizing effects.

name: Anavar / oxandrolone voice risk
summary: Oral anabolic steroid used for lean physique goals; its documented virilizing effects in women include voice deepening that can be irreversible.

name: Anabolic steroids for voice
summary: Androgens can lower the voice by acting on the larynx; documented as a virilizing side effect, and some changes may be permanent.

name: Puberty blockers delay voice change
summary: GnRH-agonist medicines that postpone puberty, which delays voice deepening and other hormone-driven changes while treatment continues.

name: HCG and clomiphene for voice
summary: Two prescription fertility drugs that raise natural testosterone, discussed online for a deeper or maintained voice.

name: Oxybutynin for sweating
summary: A bladder drug used off-label to cut sweating all over the body, for drier skin and clothes.

name: Testosterone gel (AndroGel)
summary: Prescription skin-applied testosterone for diagnosed low T, studied for gains in lean mass and drops in fat mass in hypogonadal men.

name: Nasal testosterone (Natesto)
summary: Prescription testosterone nasal gel for diagnosed low T, noted in TRT circles for possibly keeping sperm production and gonadotropins intact.

name: Oral testosterone undecanoate (Jatenzo / Kyzatrex)
summary: Prescription testosterone capsules taken by mouth for diagnosed deficiency, a needle-free TRT option aimed at supporting lean mass and less fat.

name: Testosterone pellets (Testopel)
summary: Rice-grain testosterone implants placed under the skin that release hormone for months, an established TRT option for muscle and body composition.

name: Testosterone undecanoate injection (Aveed)
summary: Long-acting testosterone injection given in a clinic every few months for diagnosed deficiency, with a REMS programme for lung oil-embolism and anaphylaxis risk.

name: Sustanon (testosterone blend)
summary: A blend of four testosterone esters in oil, discussed in bodybuilding circles for building muscle and size.

name: Cabergoline
summary: A prescription dopamine agonist that lowers prolactin, used for prolactinomas and discussed online as an add-on to hormone regimens.

name: FSH / Menopur (HMG)
aka: Menopur, menotropin, human menopausal gonadotropin, hMG, Pergonal
summary: Fertility gonadotropins (FSH, hMG) from IVF medicine, used in TRT circles to keep sperm production and testicular function going alongside testosterone.

name: Oxytocin nasal spray
aka: Intranasal oxytocin, OT spray, "love hormone" spray
summary: A bonding-hormone nasal spray used to ease social anxiety and feel more relaxed and confident in person.

name: Estradiol / HRT (feminising or menopause)
summary: The main estrogen, prescribed for menopause and feminising therapy, where it softens skin and reshapes fat distribution and body shape.
